runs.text: Breaking news. England has been occupied since four hundred and forty nine. Three tribes crossed the North Sea. The Angles, from <<ˈ|æ|ŋ|ə|l|n>>, and the Saxons, both from northern Germany. And the <<ˈ|dʒ|uː|t|s>>, from Jutland, in Denmark. Source: the monk <<ˈ|b|iː|d>>, writing in seven hundred and thirty one, dates it to four hundred and forty nine. DNA agrees: early graves in eastern England, up to seventy six percent North Sea ancestry. Even the name: England, land of the Angles. So, the obvious solution: back to Germany? Nobody says that. After one thousand five hundred years, they're home. Now, the Jews. About twelve oh eight BCE, Pharaoh <<ˈ|m|ɛ|r|n|ɛ|p|t|ɑ|z>> stone names Israel. About one thousand BCE, Jerusalem is the capital of a Jewish kingdom. Around four hundred CE, rabbis finish the Jerusalem Talmud in <<t|aɪ|ˈ|b|ɪ|r|i|ə|s>>. In the fifteen hundreds, <<ˈ|s|ɑ|f|ɛ|d>> is the centre of <<k|ə|ˈ|b|ɑ|l|ə>>. If one thousand five hundred years makes you local, what do three thousand make the Jews? Many Palestinians also have deep roots here. Both peoples are staying. The real question is how to <<ˈ|l|ɪ|v>> side by side. If you like Israel facts, follow <<n|oʊ|ˈ|ɑ|m>> <<ˈ|r|ɑː|z>> for more. So, is England still occupied?
